Never-Sold: "Ussa-Rekh, the Broker, bought hundreds of people out of their Owings on Soulrest's dock, on the shore a short way east of Lilmoth, and now he hires them out, and each freed person's carved token stays in his chest until they have worked a season for him. Heavy-Rope's crew have worked theirs and one more, and I want their tokens in their hands. There is also a bound book on his shelf with my name on it, and I want that too. The tokens lie in his chest in his house, the north house of Soulrest. The old man keeps the key on him, so I am told, and Feldril Nethri keeps about outside the locked north door. You have three ways in. You can lift the key and open the chest. You can talk Feldril Nethri into leaving the door unbarred, or the old man himself into letting the crew go. Or you can go to the berth-master, the man who finds hands for the boats and pays their hire. Heavy-Rope keeps about the shore by the docks, and he has the plan. Hear it, and better it if you can. Know what each way costs. The old man is usually in his room, near the chest, so every way through that house is under his eye, and seen, you are a thief. And remember what he is. He bought people out for thirty years and keeps nothing for himself, though one year a berth-master paid coin and a season became two. I do not ask you to hate him. I ask you for the tokens."

She gave me a leaf in her own hand to leave in the count-box for the real one, five lockpicks, and 100 gold, the Owing's first price. I'm to speak to Rows-For-Another on the channel bank north of the farm.
- Rows-For-Another told me what holds her: her leaf in the count-box inside the estate house, whose key the keeper Hulm-Tei wears; Hulm-Tei's word, which could close the Owing; and Brings-Them-Back, the fetcher on the channel north of the bank, who knows the way to her home tree. I'm to break any one of the three.
- I killed Brings-Them-Back where the channel runs on north of the bank. Nobody living knows the way to Rows-For-Another's home tree now, to fetch her back from it. I'm to tell her the channel is clear, unless I end it another way first.
